mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that suppresses corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to lower equity earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.1 percentage points signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 35% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.1pp, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% and payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% from the prior month indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 1% and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances when both HOUST and PAYEMS decline as specified, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In a low industrial production growth regime (annual growth < 0.5%), a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a manufacturing sector contraction that reduces corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO annual growth < 0.5% and INDPRO declines monthly, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 100k, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 2% from the prior month signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances when HOUST falls > 2%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.1 percentage points and a consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% annually signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when both conditions are met, or the interaction term in a regression model is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a strong retail sales growth regime (annual growth > 3%), a monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a consumer spending slowdown that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances when RSAFS annual growth > 3% and RSAFS declines monthly, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.02.
